int32_t power_mode_set(T_SYSTEM_POWER_MODE mode)

Set platform power mode.

Parameters:

mode -- [in] Platform power mode, T_SYSTEM_POWER_MODE.

Return values:

0 -- Success.

Returns:

Operation result, and will always return 0.

Returns:

int32_t power_dlps_mode_select(POWERDlpsMode mode)

Select DLPS sub mode, default value is POWER_DLPS_PFM_MODE.

Note

Switch DLPS sub mode between POWER_DLPS_PFM_MODE and POWER_DLPS_RET_MODE.

Parameters:

mode -- [in] DLPS sub mode, POWERDlpsMode.

Return values:

0 -- Success.

Returns:

Operation result, and will always return 0.

Get DLPS sub mode.

Returns:

int32_t power_mode_pause(void)

Pause low power mode. API increments a control value by 1. If the control value > 0, low power mode is not allowed to enter.

Return values:

0 -- Success.

Returns:

Operation result, and will always return 0.

int32_t power_mode_resume(void)

Resume low power mode. API decrements a control value by 1. If the control value is reduced to 0, low power mode is allowed to enter.

Return values:

0 -- Success.

Returns:

Operation result, and will always return 0.

int32_t power_check_cb_register(POWERCheckFunc func)

Register check callback function to power manager. In idle task, system will call this function each time before entering DLPS to decide whether DLPS is allowed to enter.

Parameters:

func -- [in] Check callback function, POWERCheckFunc.

Return values:

0 -- Success.

Returns:

Operation result, and will always return 0.

int32_t power_stage_cb_register(POWERStageFunc func, POWERStage stage)

Register callback function to power manager which will call it in different power stages.

Parameters:

  • func -- [in] Callback function, POWERStageFunc.

  • stage -- [in] Power stage for the callback function, POWERStage.

Return values:

0 -- Success.

Returns:

Operation result, and will always return 0.

uint32_t *power_get_refuse_reason()

Get callback function which prevents the system from entering low power mode.

Returns:

Address of callback function which prevents the system from entering low power mode.

PowerModeWakeupReason power_get_wakeup_reason()

Get wake-up reason when low power mode is exited.

Returns:

Wake-up reason, PowerModeWakeupReason.

PowerModeErrorCode power_get_error_code(void)

Get error reason which prevents system from entering low power mode.

Returns:

Error reason which prevents the system from entering low power mode, PowerModeErrorCode.

void power_get_statistics(uint32_t *wakeup_count, uint32_t *last_exit_clk, uint32_t *last_enter_clk)

Get debug information of DLPS mode.

Parameters:

  • wakeup_count -- [out] Total number of entries into DLPS.

  • last_exit_clk -- [out] Timestamp of exiting DLPS most recently, unit: 31.25us.

  • last_enter_clk -- [out] Timestamp of entering DLPS most recently, unit: 31.25us.

void power_stop_all_non_excluded_timer(void)

Stop all of the SW timers which will wake up low power mode.

Note

Before entering power down mode, all periodic wake-up timers need to be disabled before.

bool power_register_excluded_handle(void **handle, PowerModeExcludedHandleType type)

Exclude SW timer or task from low power wake list, SW timer needs to be one-shot timer.

Note

When a user wants to start a software timer or set a task delay but does not want to wake up DLPS, they can register this timer or task as an excluded timer or task. For example, if you want to create a debug timer that periodically prints the reasons for not entering DLPS in its callback function, you can register it as an excluded timer.

Parameters:

  • handle -- [in] Handle of SW timer or task.

  • type -- [in] Type of SW timer or task, PowerModeExcludedHandleType.

Return values:

  • True -- Success.

  • False -- Fail to exclude SW timer or task. This may happen when handle is NULL or heap malloc fail.

Returns:

Operation status.

bool power_unregister_excluded_handle(void **handle, PowerModeExcludedHandleType type)

Cancel exclude SW timer or task from low power wake list.

Parameters:

  • handle -- [in] Handle of timer or task.

  • type -- [in] Type of timer or task, PowerModeExcludedHandleType.

Return values:

  • True -- Success

  • False -- Fail to cancel exclude SW timer or task. This may happen when handle is NULL or handle is not found in exclude list.

Returns:

Operation status

Variables

bool (*os_register_pm_excluded_handle)(void **pp_handle, PlatformExcludedHandleType type)

Exclude SW timer or task from low power wake list, SW timer needs to be one-shot timer.

Param handle:

[in] Handle of SW timer or task.

Param type:

[in] Type of SW timer or task, refer to PlatformExcludedHandleType.

Return:

Operation status. It returns false when pp_handle is NULL or there is not enough heap to malloc.

Cancel exclude SW timer or task from low power wake list.

Param handle:

[in] Handle of timer or task.

Param type:

[in] Type of timer or task, refer to PlatformExcludedHandleType.

Return:

Operation status. It returns false when pp_handle is NULL or the pp_handle is not found.
